parts.note: Mono- means one, and MONO is a word for single-channel sound.
Taken as it stands.
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap.

explanation.surface: A traveller making a trip round some chilly land.
explanation.walkthrough: The cold country of the surface is a decoy: Monaco is famously warm, and 'cold' only supplies C.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny sovereign country on the Riviera.

clue.text: Men not raised in island capital

parts.note: Kings are pieces, or men, in chess.

indicators.note: In a down clue, 'raised' lifts NOT so it reads from the bottom up.

parts.note: Taken as it stands.

explanation.surface: Some men on an island who stay seated rather than standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' means chess pieces here, so kings; 'not raised' is NOT turned upside down in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Jamaica is the island, and Kingston its capital city.

clue.text: American flier looks to cover beaches on holiday

parts.note: To stare is to look hard.
Sands are sandy beaches.
A trip is a short holiday.

explanation.surface: A US flyer gazing down at beaches while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot or a bird; here it is something that flies from a flagpole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the American flag, which flies.

definitions.meaning: To spot something is to observe it.
A leopard's coat is covered in spots.

explanation.surface: Something noticed, like the markings on a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' flags the leopard as just one example of a spotted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to observe; a leopard has a spotted coat.

definitions.meaning: Unadventurous, mainstream, as of tastes or politics.
A jaywalker wanders into the street away from a crossing.

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second, literal reading: a jaywalker crosses the street carelessly and may be found in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: whatever avoids both extremes, like a car keeping to the centre line, is safe and ordinary; the jaywalker sense takes the phrase literally.

clue.text: Father and Holy Father atop a temple

indicators.note: In a down clue, the fathers sit 'atop' A, so they come first.

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father.
God the Father is the first person of the Trinity.
Taken as it stands.

explanation.surface: A priest and the Pope standing on top of a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy Father' usually means the Pope, but here it is GOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered temple tower in East Asia.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second.
An age is a period of time.

explanation.surface: A smart alec getting another chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise guy' usually means a smart alec; here it is meant straight, a genuinely wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym read literally: a sage is a man of great wisdom, a wise guy in the straight sense rather than the slang one.

clue.text: Mouth opening in Iraq, seeing desert

parts.note: A British slang word for the mouth, as in 'shut your ...'.

indicators.note: The 'opening' of Iraq is its first letter.

parts.note: The first letter of Iraq.

explanation.surface: Someone gaping open-mouthed at the Iraqi desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the desert in Iraq; 'opening' is not the mouth opening but the first letter of Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a large desert in Mongolia and China.

definitions.meaning: British English for a rubbish dump or landfill site.
A small extra payment left for a waiter or driver.

explanation.walkthrough: A tip is a rubbish dump in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is also a small reward for service.

parts.note: To be in is to be at home.
The other state from being at home is being away.

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone is at home or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' means the opposite of 'at home', which is AWAY, as with home and away matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases hedge a claim, meaning to some degree or after a fashion.

definitions.meaning: A verb here: to pester someone repeatedly.
A black-and-white striped mammal that forages at night.

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a request not to disturb a sleeping creature, but the clue is just two meanings side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb, to nag at someone, comes from the old sport of baiting the animal, which is a night-time forager.

clue.text: Young swimmers adept, so swimming round lake

indicators.note: Letters that are 'swimming' are moving about freely, so ADEPT SO is jumbled.

parts.note: Taken as it stands, to be jumbled.
L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps.

explanation.surface: Skilled young swimmers doing laps of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young swimmers' suggests children at a swimming club, but they are baby frogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tadpoles are young frogs and toads, and they swim.

definitions.meaning: Said literally by someone being tickled.
A scornful retort dismissing a suggestion.

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal, someone being tickled; the second is the scornful phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Don't make me laugh' is a dismissive retort, like 'pah!'.

indicators.note: The answer is 'drunk', taken in, by the words that follow.

parts.note: Across the gap: totterinG INebriate.

explanation.surface: A staggering drunk knocking back spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, so look across the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: gin, flavoured with juniper, is one of the spirits, the distilled drinks.

parts.note: Torn means split.
Taken as it stands.
A do is a party.

explanation.surface: A stormy political campaign that divided a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' and 'party' suggest politics, but the movement is of air and the party is a DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violently rotating storm.

indicators.note: 'Did you say' asks how the word sounds, not how it is written.

parts.note: When a game is finished it is over; the spelling changes but the sound stays.

explanation.surface: Asking whether the eggs have all gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the final R of over is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from biology: the Latin plural of ovum, a female egg cell.

parts.note: Food that is off has gone rotten.
A party line is a policy.

explanation.surface: A bad policy that is out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' as policy is the sense in 'the party line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-line means not connected to a network.

clue.text: Outsiders in league have penned type of clue for sport

indicators.note: The 'outsiders' of league are its first and last letters.

parts.note: The outer letters of league.
Crossword clues are either across or down.

explanation.surface: Outsiders in a sports league writing crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-reference to crosswords is the trick: 'type of clue' is ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: A horse and sheep in cryptic rearrangement?

parts.note: Taken as it stands.
A nag is an old horse.
A ram is a male sheep.

explanation.surface: Farm animals shuffled about in some puzzling way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the device itself: an anagram is the crossword solver's rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a rearrangement of letters, the staple of cryptic clues.

clue.text: Accept that's what to do with beard-grooming product?

definitions.meaning: To bear a setback without complaint, like a boxer absorbing a punch.

definitions.text: what to do with beard-grooming product?
definitions.meaning: Beard oil is applied to the chin.

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: you apply beard oil or shaving foam on the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: To take it on the chin is to accept a setback without complaint.

indicators.note: In a down clue, 'hauled up' pulls the letters upward so they read in reverse.

parts.note: A mate is a partner.

explanation.surface: A fisherman's partner nearly pulled aboard with the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' looks like a noun, as in a fishing net, but it is the verb to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to net a fish or a suspect is to catch it in a trap.

indicators.note: 'Dizzy' letters are in a spin, so LADIES is jumbled.

parts.note: Taken as it stands, to be jumbled.

explanation.surface: Giddy women working as fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' sounds like catwalk models, but it means examples to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a model, in the sense of a perfect example to copy, is what we aim at.

clue.text: Old coin, item out of reach?

parts.note: Something far away is out of reach.
An item is a thing.

explanation.surface: An old coin that has rolled somewhere you cannot get it.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the quarter-penny piece was withdrawn in 1960, so it is an old coin.

clue.text: Sadly in arrears, a labourer's given up

indicators.note: In a down clue, 'given up' sends the letters upward, reading in reverse.
The answer lies 'in' the words that follow.

parts.note: Across the gap: arrearS A LAbourer.

explanation.surface: A worker who has sadly fallen behind with payments and quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like part of the story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an expression of sadness, so it can mean sadly.

clue.text: Wild horse carrying leader on desert island

parts.note: Taken as it stands, to be jumbled.

indicators.note: The 'leader on' desert is the letter at its head.

parts.note: The first letter of desert.

explanation.surface: A wild horse carrying its leader on a desert island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' means HORSE takes D along with it into the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the largest of the Dodecanese, in the Aegean Sea off Turkey.

clue.text: Huge building, residence capturing heart of monarch

parts.note: Your place is where you live.

indicators.note: The 'heart' of monarch is its middle letter.

parts.note: A is the middle letter of monarch.

explanation.surface: A royal residence with the king at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal surface points straight at the answer, which is the definition working with the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a royal or official residence is among the grandest of large buildings.

clue.text: Military commander addressing General Assembly, first of all

indicators.note: 'First of all' takes the first letter of all the words before it.

parts.note: The first letters of those three words.

explanation.surface: A general giving a speech to the UN General Assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'General Assembly' look like the UN body, but only the initials matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical title: in the Ottoman Empire the word was a rank for a military officer.

definitions.meaning: One and only, as in the only survivor.
The underside of a shoe, a part of footwear.

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a one-of-a-kind shoe; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means only or unique; the sole is the underside of a shoe.
